Your arrows have driven deep into me; your hand weighs down on me.
Nothing in my body is healthy, because of your fury; nothing in my bones is whole, because of my sin.
My sins have closed over my head; like a heavy load, they weigh more than I can bear.
My sores are foul and rotting, all because of my own foolishness.
I am bent over, bowed down completely; I spend the whole day going about in grief.
A burning fever fills my sides, and nothing in my body is well.
I have gone numb and am crushed to the core; my heart groans, and I cry out aloud.
Lord, you see everything I long for; not one of my sighs escapes you.
My heart races; my strength has deserted me; the light of my eyes, that too is gone.
My friends and companions keep away from my sickness; even my own family stands at a distance.
Those who want my life set traps; those who want to hurt me speak of destroying me and mutter lies all day long.
But I act as if I were deaf and hear nothing, as if I were mute and could not open my mouth.
I have turned into someone who hears nothing and has no answer to give.
LORD, my hope is fixed on you; you are the one who will answer, Lord my God.
For I said, “Do not let them enjoy my fall; when my foot slips, they lord it over me.”
I am on the edge of collapse, and my pain never leaves my sight.
I openly admit my guilt; my sin weighs on me with dread.
Meanwhile my enemies are full of life and strength; many hate me for no good reason.
Those who return evil for kindness act as my accusers, because I go after what is good.
Do not abandon me, LORD; my God, do not stay far from me.
Be quick to help me, Lord, my salvation.

fields.title: Psalm 39
fields.body_html:
My life is only a breath

For the music director. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

I made up my mind: “I will be careful how I live, so that my tongue does not lead me into sin. I will keep my mouth muzzled for as long as the wicked stand before me.”
I said nothing at all; I held my peace, even from saying good, and my pain grew sharper.
Inside me my heart was burning; as I brooded, it flared into fire, and at last I spoke:
LORD, let me know my end and how many days are measured out for me; let me understand how short-lived I am.
See, you have made my days only a few hand widths long; my whole lifetime is as nothing in your sight. Every human being, however firmly they stand, is only a breath. Selah
Truly, people go about like shadows; their busy noise is all for nothing; they pile things up, not knowing who will collect them.
So then, Lord, what is left for me to wait for? My hope rests on you.
Rescue me from all my rebellious acts; do not make me something fools laugh at.
I stay silent and say nothing, because this is your doing.
Take your blow away from me; I am worn out by the force of your hand.
You punish people for their wrongs with rebukes, and like a moth you eat away what they love most. Every human being is only a breath. Selah
LORD, hear what I pray; turn your ear to my plea for help, and do not keep silent when I weep. I am only a guest with you, a foreigner passing through, just like my ancestors before me.
Turn your gaze from me, and let me find joy again before I leave and am no longer here.

fields.title: Psalm 40
fields.body_html:
A new song, then a cry for help

For the music director. Of David. A psalm.

I waited and kept on waiting for the LORD, and he bent down toward me and listened to my cry for help.
He drew me up from the roaring pit, out of the clinging mud; he planted my feet on a rock and steadied my steps.
He gave me a new song to sing, a hymn for our God. Many people will look on and be filled with awe, and they will put their trust in the LORD.
How blessed are those who make the LORD their trust, who do not turn to the arrogant or to those who wander off after lies!
LORD my God, you have done so many things, your wonders and your plans for us; no one can compare with you! If I tried to tell them all and speak of them, there would be more than I could count.
You took no pleasure in sacrifice and offering, but you opened my ears; you did not ask for burnt offerings or sin offerings.
Then I said, “Here I come! What I must do is written down for me in the scroll of the book.
My God, I love to do what you want; your instruction is deep inside me.”
In the great assembly I have announced the good news of righteousness. I have not held my lips back; you know it, LORD.
Your justice I did not keep shut up in my heart; I talked of how faithful you are and how you rescue. Your loyal love and your truth I did not hide from the great assembly.
And you, LORD, will not hold back your tender mercy from me; your loyal love and your truth will guard me always.
Troubles too many to count have closed in around me; my sins have caught up with me, and I cannot see. They outnumber the hairs on my head, and my courage has left me.
LORD, be willing to rescue me! LORD, hurry and help me!
Let those who hunt for my life to snatch it away be shamed and confounded, all of them; let those who wish me harm be driven back and humiliated.
Let those who jeer at me, “Aha! Aha!”, be stunned by their own shame.
But may everyone who looks for you shout for joy and find gladness in you; may those who love to see you save never stop saying, “How great the LORD is!”
As for me, I am poor and in need; may the Lord keep me in mind. You are the one who helps me and sets me free; my God, do not be slow!

fields.title: Psalm 41
fields.body_html:
Betrayed by a friend, upheld by God

For the music director. A psalm of David.

How blessed are those who care about the weak! When trouble comes, the LORD will rescue them.
The LORD will protect them and keep them alive; they will be counted blessed in the land. Do not hand them over to the will of their enemies!
The LORD will hold them up on their sickbed; when they are ill, you turn their whole bed of sickness to health.
I said, “LORD, show me grace! Heal me, because it is you I have sinned against.”
My enemies say cruel things about me: “When will he die and be wiped from memory?”
When any of them come to visit me, they say what they do not mean, while inside they gather up bad news; then they go out and spread it.
All who hate me whisper together about me; they plot harm against me, saying,
“Some deadly thing has been poured into him; now that he is down, he will never get up again.”
Even the friend I was at peace with, the one I trusted, who shared my bread, has turned his heel against me.
But you, LORD, show me grace and lift me up, so that I can pay them back.
This is how I know you are pleased with me: my enemy does not get to cheer in triumph over me.
As for me, you keep hold of me in my integrity and let me stand before your face for all time.
May the LORD, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! Amen and amen.

fields.title: Psalm 42
fields.body_html:
Thirsty for the living God

For the music director. A maskil of the sons of Korah.

Like a doe that longs for running streams, I long for you, God, with all my being.
I am thirsty for God, the living God. When may I come and stand before God’s face?
Day and night I have fed on my tears, while all day long people ask me, “Where is your God?”
I pour out my heart as I call these things to mind: how I walked with the crowd and led them up to God’s house, among shouts of joy and songs of thanks, a great crowd celebrating the feast.
Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, for the rescue that comes from his presence.
My God, I am bent low inside; so I will remember you here in the Jordan country and on the peaks of Hermon, on Mount Mizar.
One deep calls out to another at the roar of your cascades; all your breaking waves and rollers have gone over my head.
By day the LORD sends out his loyal love, and at night his song stays with me, a prayer to the God who gives me life.
I cry out to God, my rock: “Why have you put me out of your mind? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?”
My foes mock me with a taunt that crushes my bones, while all day long they ask me, “Where is your God?”
Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.

fields.title: Psalm 43
fields.body_html:
Send out your light and truth

Give judgment for me, God, and take up my case against a nation without loyalty; save me from people who lie and do wrong.
For you are God, my fortress. Why have you pushed me away? Why do I walk about dressed in grief while the enemy presses me hard?
Let your light and your truth go out to guide me; may they lead me up to your holy mountain, to the place where you live.
Then I will come up to God’s altar, to God, who is my gladness and my joy, and with the lyre I will give you thanks, God, my God.
Why are you bent so low, my soul? Why this unrest inside me? Wait for God in hope; I will give him thanks again, the one who saves me, my God.

fields.title: Psalm 44
fields.body_html:
Faithful, yet crushed: wake up, Lord

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil.

God, our own ears have heard it; our ancestors told us of the deeds you did when they lived, in times long past.
With your own hand you drove out nations and planted our ancestors in their place; you struck down peoples and let our ancestors spread out.
Their own swords did not win them the land; their own strength did not bring them rescue. Your right hand did it, your arm, and the shining of your face, because you took delight in them.
You alone are my King, God; give the order for Jacob’s victories.
Through you we gore our enemies like a bull; through your name we stamp down those who attack us.
I do not rely on my own bow, and my sword cannot save me.
No, it is you who rescued us from our enemies and put to shame those who hate us.
God has been our boast the whole day long, and to your name we will give praise for all time. Selah
Yet you have thrown us aside and disgraced us; you do not go into battle with our troops.
You made us retreat before the enemy, and those who hate us have helped themselves to our goods.
You hand us over like sheep to be eaten, and you have spread us out among the nations.
You sell off your own people for next to nothing; their price has not made you any richer.
You have made us a disgrace in the eyes of our neighbors, a joke and a laughingstock to all around us.
You have turned our name into a proverb among the nations; the peoples shake their heads at us.
All day long I see my disgrace, and shame is written over my face,
because of the voice of those who taunt and mock, because of the sight of the enemy bent on revenge.
All this has fallen on us, yet we have not put you out of mind or broken faith with your covenant.
Our hearts have not turned away, and our feet have not wandered from your road,
yet you have crushed us in a place where only jackals live, and wrapped us in deathly darkness.
Had we forgotten our God’s name, or lifted our hands in prayer to a foreign god,
would not God have searched it out? For he knows what is hidden in the heart.
Because we belong to you, we are being killed all day long; we are looked on as sheep marked for the butcher.
Wake up, Lord! Why are you sleeping? Rise from your sleep! Do not cast us off forever!
Why do you turn your face away and forget how we suffer and are oppressed?
We are bowed down into the dust; our bodies are pressed flat against the ground.
Rise up and come to our help! Set us free because of your loyal love.

fields.title: Psalm 45
fields.body_html:
A wedding song for the king

For the music director. On shoshannim. Of the sons of Korah. A maskil. A love song.

A lovely theme has set my heart astir; I offer my verses to the king, and my tongue runs like the pen of an expert scribe.
You are more handsome than anyone else; grace pours from your lips; that is why God has blessed you forever.
Strap your sword to your side, mighty warrior, in your splendor and your majesty!
In your majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility and justice; let your right hand show you deeds that inspire awe.
Your arrows are sharp; peoples fall beneath you; they pierce the hearts of the king’s enemies.
Your throne, God, lasts for ever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter that rules rightly.
You love justice and hate evil; that is why God, your God, has anointed you, rather than your companions, with the oil of gladness.
Your robes all breathe out myrrh and aloes and cassia; the sound of strings from ivory-inlaid palaces brings you joy.
Princesses are among the ladies of your court; at your right hand stands the queen, adorned with gold from Ophir.
Hear me, daughter, take note and listen closely: leave behind your own people and your family home,
then the king will long for your beauty. He is your lord; bow down to him.
Tyre’s daughter will come with a gift; the wealthiest of the people will try to win your favor.
The princess waits within, all splendid; her gown is woven with gold.
In bright embroidered robes she is led to the king, with her maiden companions following, brought to you.
Amid joy and celebration they are escorted in, and they go into the king’s palace.
Where your fathers once stood, your sons will stand; you will set them up as princes over all the land.
I will make your name remembered from one generation to the next; so the nations will give you thanks for all time.

fields.title: Psalm 46
fields.body_html:
God is with us in the shaking world

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. On alamoth. A song.

God is a shelter and a strength for us, a help always close at hand in times of distress.
So we will not be afraid, even if the earth is overturned and the mountains slide down into the depths of the sea,
when its waters roar and churn and the mountains shudder as the sea heaves. Selah
There is a river; its channels bring joy to God’s city, the sacred home of the Most High.
God is in the middle of the city; nothing will topple it. God will come to its aid as the morning breaks.
Nations were in turmoil and kingdoms shook; he thundered, and the earth melted away.
The LORD of Armies is on our side; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah
Come, look at the deeds of the LORD, the havoc he has worked across the earth.
He puts an end to wars as far as the earth reaches; he snaps the bow, splits the spear, and sets the war wagons on fire.
“Stop, and acknowledge that I am God. Among the nations I will be lifted high; over all the earth I will be lifted high.”
The LORD of Armies is on our side; the God of Jacob is our high fortress. Selah

fields.title: Psalm 47
fields.body_html:
God goes up as King of all the earth

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

All you peoples, clap your hands! Raise a shout to God with ringing cries of joy!
For the LORD Most High inspires awe; he is the great King who rules the whole earth.
He brings peoples under our rule and lays nations at our feet.
He picked out our heritage for us, the glory of Jacob, the one he loved. Selah
God has gone up amid shouting; the LORD has gone up as the ram’s horn sounds.
Make music to God, make music! Make music to our King, make music!
For God reigns as King of all the earth; make music with a skillful psalm.
God now rules as King over the nations; upon his holy throne God sits.
The princes of the peoples come together to be the people of Abraham’s God. For the shields of the earth are God’s; he is raised high above all.

fields.title: Psalm 48
fields.body_html:
Zion, the city of the great King

A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.

The LORD is great and deserves all praise in the city of our God, on his holy mountain.
Mount Zion rises in beauty, the delight of the whole earth; it is the true heights of Zaphon, the great King’s city.
Within the city’s strongholds God has proved himself a high refuge.
Look: the kings gathered their armies and marched on together.
They looked, and were stunned; they panicked and ran.
There they were seized with shaking, with pangs like a woman giving birth.
With a wind from the east you wreck the ships of Tarshish.
What we had heard, we have now seen with our own eyes in the city of the LORD of Armies, the city of our God: God will make it stand firm forever. Selah
God, we have reflected on your loyal love here inside your temple.
Your praise, God, matches your name and spreads to the far ends of the earth; your right hand overflows with justice.
Let Mount Zion be glad, and the towns of Judah celebrate, because you judge rightly.
Make a circuit of Zion and walk all the way around; count up its towers,
take careful note of its walls, walk through its strongholds, so that you can tell the generation to come
that this is God, our God forever and always; he will be our guide until we die.

fields.title: Psalm 49
fields.body_html:
No one can buy a way out of death

For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

Listen to this, all you nations; pay attention, everyone who lives in the world,
the humble and the great, the rich and the poor together.
What I say will be wise; what my heart has pondered will give insight.
I will listen closely to a proverb; to the music of the lyre I will lay open my riddle.
Why should I be afraid in evil times, when the wrongdoing of those who dog my steps closes in on me,
people who rely on their money and brag about how rich they are?
No one can ever buy back the life of another, or pay God the price for that person’s life,
for the price of a life is far too high, and no payment could ever be enough,
so that anyone could live on forever and never see the grave.
Anyone can see it: wise people die, and fools and dullards perish with them, handing over their wealth to others.
They imagine their houses will last forever, their homes for all generations; they have named whole estates after themselves.
Yet no one, however honored, stays for long; humans are no different from animals that die.
Such is the road of the foolishly self-assured, and of those who come after them and like what they say. Selah
Like sheep they are herded into Sheol, and Death is their shepherd. The upright will rule over them when morning comes; their bodies will waste away in Sheol, far from their grand houses.
But God will pay the ransom for my life and free it from Sheol’s grip, for he will take me. Selah
Do not be alarmed when someone gets rich and their household gains in wealth and honor,
for when they die they can take none of it with them; their splendor will not follow them down.
Though in life they count themselves blessed — and people praise you when you prosper —
they will go to join the generation of their ancestors, who will never again see the light.
A person held in honor who does not understand is no different from animals that die.

fields.title: Psalm 50
fields.body_html:
God brings his people to court

A psalm of Asaph.

The Mighty One, God, the LORD, has spoken; he has called to the whole earth, from the sunrise to the sunset.
God has blazed out from Zion, the city of flawless beauty.
Our God is coming, and he will not stay silent; a fire consumes all in his path, and a fierce storm rages on every side.
He calls heaven above and earth below as witnesses, as he judges his people:
“Bring together before me my loyal people, who sealed my covenant with a sacrifice.”
The heavens make known his justice, because it is God who sits as judge. Selah
“Pay attention, my people, for I am about to speak; I am bringing testimony against you, Israel. I am God, your God.
I do not find fault with you over your sacrifices; your burnt offerings are always in front of me.
I will not accept a young bull from your household, or male goats out of your sheepfolds.
For all the creatures of the woods belong to me, and so do the herds grazing over a thousand hills.
I know every bird of the high hills; whatever stirs in the open country is in my keeping.
Were I ever hungry, you are not the one I would tell, since the world and all it holds are mine.
Am I one who eats the meat of bulls, or drinks the blood of goats?
Offer thanksgiving to God as your sacrifice, and keep the vows you made to the Most High,
and call to me when trouble comes; I will set you free, and you will give me glory.”
But to the wicked God says: “What business do you have reciting my decrees, or mouthing the words of my covenant?
You hate to be corrected, and you toss my words over your shoulder.
You see a thief and are happy to go along with him; you share in what adulterers do.
You let your mouth run free to do harm, and your tongue weaves lies.
You sit around speaking against your brother; you smear the name of your own mother’s son.
You did these things and I said nothing, so you imagined I was no different from you. Now I will rebuke you and lay out the case before your eyes.
Now take this to heart, all of you who forget God, or I will tear you apart like a lion, and no one will be able to save you.
Whoever offers thanks as a sacrifice gives me honor, and whoever walks the right road, I will let them see how God saves.”

fields.title: Psalm 51
fields.body_html:
Create a pure heart in me

For the music director. A psalm of David, when the prophet Nathan came to him after he had slept with Bathsheba.

God, be gracious to me in keeping with your loyal love;
in the fullness of your compassion,
wipe away my rebellious acts.
Scrub me completely clean of my guilt,
and purify me from my sin.
I myself know my rebellious acts,
and my sin is never out of my sight.
I have sinned against you, against you alone,
and done what you see as evil.
So you are shown to be right in your sentence
and pure in your judgment.
Indeed, guilt was with me when I was born;
sin was there when my mother conceived me.
Yet you long for truth deep within,
and in my secret self you make wisdom known to me.
Take away my sin with hyssop, and I will be pure;
when you wash me, I will be whiter than snow.
Fill my ears with gladness and joy;
let the bones you crushed dance.
Turn your face away from my sins,
and erase all my guilt.
God, create a pure heart for me,
and make my spirit new and steady inside me.
Do not drive me away from your presence,
and do not withdraw your Holy Spirit from me.
Give back to me the gladness of your salvation,
and keep me steady with a willing spirit.
I will teach rebels your paths,
and sinners will come home to you.
Rescue me, God, from the guilt of the blood I have shed,
God who saves me;
then my tongue will ring out with your righteousness.
Lord, open my lips to speak,
and I will make your praise known.
Sacrifice is not what you desire, or I would offer it;
a burnt offering does not please you.
The sacrifices that God accepts are a broken spirit.
A heart that is broken and crushed,
God, you will never reject.
In your goodwill be kind to Zion,
and raise up Jerusalem’s walls.
Then you will welcome sacrifices offered in righteousness, burnt offerings and whole offerings;
then young bulls will be brought up onto your altar.

fields.title: Psalm 52
fields.body_html:
The boaster and the olive tree

For the music director. A maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite went and informed Saul, telling him, “David has gone to Ahimelech’s house.”

Why brag about evil, you mighty warrior?
God’s loyal love goes on all day long.
Your tongue devises ruin;
it cuts like a honed razor, you schemer of lies.
You prefer evil to good,
and a lie to an honest word. Selah
You love every word that devours,
you lying tongue.
But God will bring you down for good;
he will seize you and drag you out of your tent,
and pull you up by the roots from the land of the living. Selah
The righteous will see it and be filled with awe;
they will laugh at him and say,
“Look at the man who would not take God as his fortress!
He relied on his great wealth
and looked for safety in the ruin he caused.”
I, though, am like an olive tree in full leaf in God’s house;
I rely on God’s loyal love forever and ever.
I will thank you forever for what you have done;
before your loyal people I will wait in hope on your name,
because it is good.

fields.title: Psalm 53
fields.body_html:
Not one does good

For the music director. On mahalath. A maskil of David.

Fools tell themselves, “There is no God.”
They are rotten through and through;
their wrongdoing is detestable.
Not one of them does good.
From heaven God looks down on the human race
to see whether anyone is wise,
anyone who is looking for God.
Everyone has turned away; all alike have gone bad.
No one does good,
not a single one.
Have they learned nothing, these evildoers?
They devour my people as if they were eating bread,
and they never call on God.
Terror gripped them there, where there had been nothing to fear,
for God scattered the bones of the army camped against you.
You brought them to shame, because God had thrown them aside.
If only Zion would send Israel its rescue!
When God turns back the fortunes of his people,
let Jacob shout for joy and Israel be glad.

fields.title: Psalm 54
fields.body_html:
God, save me by your name

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David, when the people of Ziph came and said to Saul, “David is hiding among us, is he not?”

God, save me by your name;
by your strength take up my cause.
God, listen to my prayer;
pay attention to what I am saying.
For outsiders have risen up against me,
and violent people are hunting for my life;
they give God no thought. Selah
But see, God comes to my aid;
the Lord is the one who holds my life up.
He will turn back the harm on my enemies;
because you are faithful, wipe them out.
I will offer you a sacrifice of my own free will;
LORD, I will thank you and honor your name, for it is good.
For he has pulled me out of every trouble,
and my eyes have seen my enemies defeated.

fields.title: Psalm 55
fields.body_html:
Betrayed by a close friend

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.

God, listen to my prayer;
do not close your eyes to my plea.
Listen to me and answer me.
My worries leave me no rest, and I groan aloud,
at the shouting of the enemy
and the crushing weight of the wicked;
for they bring trouble crashing down on me,
and in their anger they nurse a grudge against me.
My heart twists in pain inside me;
the dread of death has come down on me.
Fear and trembling take hold of me;
I am wrapped in horror.
I said, “If only I had a dove’s wings!
I would fly off and settle somewhere far away.
See, I would run far off
and spend my nights in the wilderness. Selah
I would hurry to a refuge of my own,
away from the raging wind and the storm.”
Lord, bring them to nothing and split their speech,
because I have seen violence and quarreling all through the city.
Day and night violence and strife make their rounds on its walls,
and evil and misery fill the city.
Ruin is at its center;
cruelty and lies never leave its public square.
The one who mocks me is not an enemy, or I could bear it;
the one who lords it over me is not someone who hates me,
or I could keep out of his way.
But it is you, a man of my own standing,
my friend and my trusted companion,
we used to share our hearts as friends,
and we walked with the crowd at the house of God.
Let death catch them off guard;
let them drop alive into Sheol,
for evil lives in their homes and deep within them.
But I will cry out to God,
and the LORD will come to save me.
At evening, at morning and at noon I pour out my troubles and groan aloud,
and he hears me.
He has ransomed my life and brought me safely out of the battle waged on me,
for many were lined up against me.
God, enthroned since ancient times, will hear and bring them low,
for they never change their ways and they do not fear God. Selah
My friend has raised his hand against those who were at peace with him;
he has broken his covenant.
His talk was as smooth as cream, but his heart was set on war;
his words flowed more gently than oil, yet each was a drawn sword.
Hand over to the LORD whatever weighs on you, and he will hold you up;
never will he allow the righteous to stumble and fall.
But you, God, will send them down to the deepest pit;
killers and liars will not see even half their years.
As for me, I will trust in you.

fields.title: Psalm 56
fields.body_html:
When I am afraid, I trust

For the music director. On yonath elem rechokim. Of David. A miktam, when the Philistines seized him in Gath.

God, show me grace, for people trample on me;
all day long they fight me and press me hard.
My enemies hound me all day long;
many are fighting against me in their arrogance.
On the day fear strikes,
I will rely on you.
With God I celebrate his promise;
in God I have put my trust and will not be afraid.
What can mere flesh do to me?
All day long they twist what I say;
every plan they make is for my harm.
They band together and hide;
they watch my every step,
eager to take my life.
Will they get away with such wickedness?
God, in anger throw down the nations.
You yourself have kept count of my wanderings;
store my tears in your flask.
Are they not already in your record?
When I call for help, my enemies will retreat;
this much I know, God is on my side.
In God, whose promise I celebrate,
in the LORD, whose promise I celebrate,
in God I have put my trust; I will not fear.
What can a mere human do to me?
God, I am bound by the vows I made to you;
I will pay them with offerings of thanks to you.
For you have rescued me from death
and kept my feet from slipping,
so that I can walk with God
in the light of the living.

fields.title: Psalm 57
fields.body_html:
Shelter in the shadow of your wings

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, when he fled from Saul into the cave.

Show me grace, God, show me grace,
for I have made you my refuge;
I will shelter under the shadow of your wings
until the time of ruin is over.
I call on God Most High,
the God who carries out his plan for me.
He will reach down from heaven and rescue me,
and disgrace the one who hounds me;
God will send forth his loyal love and his faithfulness. Selah
I am surrounded by lions; I must lie down among people who devour like beasts.
Their teeth are spear points and arrows,
their tongues a sharpened sword.
God, be lifted high above the heavens;
let your glory spread over all the earth.
They laid a net for my steps, and I sank down in despair;
they hollowed out a pit ahead of me,
and into it they fell. Selah
My heart is firm, God, my heart is firm;
I will sing and play songs of praise.
Rouse yourself, my soul!
Come awake, harp and lyre!
I will wake up the dawn.
Lord, I will thank you before all peoples;
I will sing your praise in every nation.
For your loyal love towers up to the heavens,
and your faithfulness rises to the clouds.
God, be lifted high above the heavens;
let your glory spread over all the earth.

fields.title: Psalm 58
fields.body_html:
A God who judges the earth

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam.

You gods, do you really speak what is right?
Do you judge human beings fairly?
No, in your hearts you plan wrong,
and on earth your hands deal out violence by weight.
From the womb the wicked have turned aside;
from birth those who tell lies have wandered off.
Their poison is like a snake’s poison,
like a cobra that is deaf and stops up its ear,
so that it does not hear the voice of the charmers,
however skilled the one who weaves the spell.
God, smash the teeth in their mouths;
LORD, rip out the young lions’ fangs!
Let them drain away like water running off;
when they take aim with their arrows, let the shafts be snapped.
May they be like a snail that turns to slime as it moves,
like a baby born dead, who has not looked on the sun.
Sooner than your pots can sense the thorn fire,
green or blazing, he will sweep it all away in a storm.
The righteous will be glad when they see justice repaid;
they will bathe their feet in the wicked’s blood.
Then people will say, “Yes, the righteous do receive a reward;
yes, a God does judge on the earth.”

fields.title: Psalm 59
fields.body_html:
Rescue from enemies who prowl at night

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A miktam, from the time when Saul sent men to watch David’s house in order to kill him.

Rescue me from my enemies, my God;
lift me high out of reach of those who rise against me.
Rescue me from those who do evil;
save me from men who shed blood.
Look, they lie in ambush for my life;
powerful men band together against me,
though I have not rebelled or sinned, LORD.
Through no fault of mine they rush to take up their places.
Wake up, come to meet me, and look!
LORD God of Armies, God of Israel,
rise up and call all the nations to account;
have no pity on any who plot evil in their treachery. Selah
At nightfall they return,
snarling like dogs as they roam the city.
Look how their mouths gush with insults;
their lips are swords,
for they say, “Who will hear?”
But you, LORD, laugh at them;
you hold all the nations in derision.
Against his strength I will keep watch for you,
for God is my high fortress.
My God of loyal love will go before me;
God will let me look down on my foes.
Do not kill them outright, in case my people forget;
by your power send them staggering and bring them low,
Lord, our shield.
Every word from their lips is sin in their mouths;
let them be snared by their own pride,
for the cursing and lying they speak.
Destroy them in your anger, destroy them until they are gone,
so that people will know that God rules over Jacob
to the ends of the earth. Selah
At nightfall they return,
snarling like dogs as they roam the city.
They roam about for food,
and if they are not filled, they stay out all night.
But I will sing of your might,
and at daybreak I will shout for joy over your loyal love,
for you have been my high fortress,
a place to flee to when I was in trouble.
My Strength, I will make music to you,
for God is my high fortress, my God of loyal love.

fields.title: Psalm 60
fields.body_html:
Help against the foe after defeat

For the music director. On shushan eduth. A miktam of David, for teaching, when he fought against Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab came back and struck down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.

God, you have thrown us off and burst through our walls.
You have been angry; turn to us again!
You made the land shudder and tore it apart;
mend its cracks, for it is giving way.
You let your people see hard things;
you made us drink a wine that sent us reeling.
For those who fear you, you have raised a banner to rally to,
out of reach of the bow. Selah
So that those you love may be set free,
bring rescue with your right hand and answer me!
God has spoken from his holy place: “I will rejoice
as I share out Shechem
and mark off the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead belongs to me, Manasseh is mine;
Ephraim is the helmet on my head,
Judah the staff of my rule.
Moab is my washing bowl;
on Edom I toss my sandal;
Philistia, raise your shout to me!”
Who will take me into the walled city?
Who will guide me all the way to Edom?
Is it not you, God, who rejected us
and no longer march out with our armies?
Help us against the enemy,
for any rescue that people can bring is useless.
With God on our side we will fight with courage;
he is the one who will crush our foes underfoot.

fields.title: Psalm 61
fields.body_html:
Lead me to the rock higher than I

For the music director. On a stringed instrument. Of David.

God, hear my loud cry;
pay attention to my prayer.
From the far edge of the earth I call to you while my heart fails;
lead me up onto a rock too high for me to climb.
For you have been my shelter,
a strong tower to hold off the enemy.
Let me live as a guest in your tent for all time;
let me find refuge under the cover of your wings. Selah
God, you have heard the promises I made;
you have granted me the share that belongs to those who honor your name.
Add days upon days to the king’s life;
may his years go on through generation after generation.
May he sit on his throne in God’s presence forever;
let loyal love and faithfulness be appointed as his guards.
Then I will make music to your name for all time
as I keep my vows day after day.

fields.title: Psalm 62
fields.body_html:
Wait quietly for God alone

For the music director. According to Jeduthun. A psalm of David.

I am quiet before God alone;
my rescue comes from him.
Only he is my rock who saves me, my high fortress;
I will not be badly shaken.
How long will you all rush at one man to batter him down,
as if he were a leaning wall,
a fence about to fall?
Their only plan is to bring him down from his high place; they love what is false.
Their lips speak blessing
while inside they curse. Selah
Be still before God alone, my soul,
for he is the source of my hope.
Only he is my rock who saves me, my high fortress;
I will not be shaken.
On God rest my rescue and my honor;
the rock of my strength and my shelter are in God.
People, rely on him in every season;
empty your hearts out before him.
God is our shelter. Selah
Ordinary people are only a breath, and the great are a lie;
put on the scales, they rise;
all together they weigh less than a breath.
Do not lean on what you gain by force, or let robbery fill you with empty hopes;
if wealth multiplies,
do not give your heart to it.
God has spoken one thing,
and I have heard it twice over:
that strength is God’s,
and to you, Lord, belongs loyal love;
for you pay all people back for what they have done.

fields.title: Psalm 63
fields.body_html:
Thirsting for God in a dry land

A psalm of David, when he was in the wilderness of Judah.

God, you are my God, and I search hard for you.
My whole self thirsts for you; my body aches for you
in a dry and worn-out land with no water.
So I have gazed on you in the holy place
and seen your might and your glory.
Your loyal love is worth more than life,
so my lips will sing your praise.
So I will bless you all my life;
I will raise my hands as I call on your name.
I will be filled as with a feast of rich food,
and with shouts of joy on my lips my mouth will sing your praise.
When I call you to mind as I lie in bed,
I muse on you through the hours of the night.
You have come to my help,
and under the shadow of your wings I sing out for joy.
I hold fast to you;
your right hand keeps me safe.
But those who hunt my life to ruin it
will sink into the lowest places of the earth.
The sword will have them in its grip,
and jackals will take them as their share.
But the king will find his joy in God;
all who take their oaths in his name will celebrate,
while liars will have their mouths shut.

fields.title: Psalm 64
fields.body_html:
God’s arrows against secret plotters

For the music director. A psalm of David.

God, listen to me as I pour out my complaint;
keep me safe from the enemy I dread.
Shelter me from the wicked when they plot together in secret,
from the restless crowd of those who do evil,
who grind their tongues sharp as a sword
and fit bitter words to the bow like arrows,
to fire from hiding at the blameless;
all at once they let fly, without any fear.
They make each other bold in their evil scheme
and talk of setting traps where none can see;
they say, “Who will notice them?”
They search out crimes and say,
“We have a flawless scheme, thoroughly thought out!”
How deep are the thoughts and the heart of a human being!
But God lets fly an arrow at them;
in an instant they are wounded.
Their own words trip them and bring them down;
everyone who sees them shakes their head.
Then everyone is struck with awe;
they announce what God has done
and think deeply about his deeds.
May the righteous be glad in the LORD and make him their refuge;
may all whose hearts are true give praise.

fields.title: Psalm 65
fields.body_html:
Praise for the God who sends rain

For the music director. A psalm of David. A song.

For you, God, in Zion, silence is praise,
and to you vows will be kept.
You hear prayer;
all people will come before you.
Wrongdoings overwhelm me,
but you cover over our rebellions.
How blessed are those whom you choose and draw close, to dwell in your courts!
May we feast on the goodness of your house,
your holy temple.
With deeds that inspire awe you answer us in righteousness, God of our rescue,
trusted by all the ends of the earth
and by those on the far-off seas,
who fixed the mountains in place by his power,
wearing might like a belt,
who quiets the thunder of the seas and the crash of their waves,
and the uproar of the nations.
Those who live at the far edges of the world stand in awe of your wonders;
you make the lands of sunrise and sunset sing for joy.
You pay a visit to the earth and soak it with rain; you make it richly fertile.
God’s channel is brimming with water;
you supply people with grain,
for this is how you have prepared the land.
Pouring water into its furrows and pressing down its ridges,
you make the soil soft with rain showers
and bless all that springs up from it.
You set a crown on the year of your goodness,
and the tracks of your chariot drip with richness.
Even the pastures of the open country drip with plenty,
and the hills put on joy like a belt.
Flocks cover the pastures like clothing,
and grain wraps the valleys;
they cry out in triumph, yes, they sing!

fields.title: Psalm 66
fields.body_html:
Come and see what God has done

For the music director. A song. A psalm.

Raise a shout to God, all the earth!
Make music to the honor of his name;
give him praise that is full of glory!
Say to God, “How fearsome are your deeds!
Because your strength is so great,
your enemies cower and fawn before you.
The whole earth bows low to you and sings to you;
they make music to your name.” Selah
Come and look at the works of God,
how fearsome his dealings are with humankind!
He changed the sea into dry ground;
they crossed the river on foot.
There let us rejoice in him!
He reigns in his power forever,
and his eyes watch closely over the nations.
Let no rebels raise themselves up. Selah
Peoples of the world, bless our God,
and make the sound of his praise ring out,
the one who keeps us alive
and has not let our feet stumble.
For you have put us to the test, God;
you have refined us the way silver is refined.
You led us into the trap;
you laid a heavy weight on our backs.
You let mere mortals ride roughshod over our heads;
we came through fire and water,
but you led us out into overflowing plenty.
I will enter your house with whole burnt offerings
and keep my vows to you,
the promises that burst from my lips,
that my mouth made in my time of distress.
I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals, along with the smoke of rams rising to you;
I will sacrifice bulls together with goats. Selah
Come, listen, all who revere God;
let me recount the things he has done for me.
With my own mouth I called to him,
and praise to lift him high was ready under my tongue.
The Lord would not have heard me
if I had kept wrongdoing in my heart.
Yet God has indeed heard me;
he has paid close attention as I prayed.
Blessed be God,
who has not pushed my prayer aside
or taken his loyal love away from me!

fields.title: Psalm 67
fields.body_html:
May all the peoples praise you, God

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.

May God show us grace and bless us;
may he let the light of his face shine on us. Selah
Then the earth will know your ways,
and every nation your power to save.
May the peoples give you thanks, God;
may every people give you thanks!
Let the nations celebrate and shout with joy,
because you judge the peoples fairly
and lead the nations across the earth. Selah
May the peoples give you thanks, God;
may every people give you thanks!
The earth has brought forth its crops;
God, our own God, will bless us.
God is going to bless us,
and all the far corners of the earth will hold him in awe.

fields.title: Psalm 68
fields.body_html:
God marches from Sinai to Zion

For the music director. Of David. A psalm. A song.

Let God rise up and his enemies scatter;
let all who hate him run from his presence.
Blow them away as smoke is blown away;
as wax melts in front of the flames,
may the wicked come to nothing in God’s presence.
But let the righteous be glad and celebrate before God;
let them be overjoyed.
Sing to God, make music to his name;
prepare a highway for the one who rides through the deserts.
The LORD is his name; celebrate before him!
From his holy dwelling
God acts as father to orphans and defender of widows.
God gives the lonely a home to live in;
he leads prisoners out into well-being,
but rebels stay in a sunbaked land.
God, you went out at the head of your people;
you strode through the desert. Selah
The earth trembled and the sky streamed with rain before God,
the God of Sinai;
before God, Israel’s God.
God, you sent showers of generous rain;
when your land was worn out, you restored it.
Your flock found a home there;
out of your goodness, God, you made ready what the afflicted needed.
The Lord speaks the word,
and a great army of women spreads the good news:
“Kings with their armies run, they run away,
and the woman who stayed at home shares out the spoil.”
Even if you men lie among the sheep pens,
there are a dove’s wings sheathed in silver,
its feathers shining with pale gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings across the land,
snow came down on Zalmon.
Mount Bashan is a mighty mountain;
Mount Bashan is a mountain of many peaks.
Why do you glare in envy, you many-peaked mountains,
at the mountain God longed for as his home?
There the LORD will live for all time.
God’s chariots number twenty thousand, thousands more again;
the Lord is among them, and Sinai has come into the holy place.
You climbed to the heights and led away a band of captives;
you accepted tribute from human beings,
even from those who rebelled, so that the LORD God could make a home there.
Blessed be the Lord, who carries our load day after day,
the God who saves us. Selah
This God of ours is a God of rescues;
the Lord GOD holds the ways of escape from death.
Yes, God will smash the skulls of his enemies,
the hairy scalps of those who keep walking in their guilt.
The Lord has spoken: “I will fetch them back from Bashan,
fetch them back from the deepest sea,
so that you may plunge your feet in blood,
and your dogs’ tongues may have their share of the enemy.”
Your solemn marches have been seen, God,
the marches of my God, my King, as he enters the holy place.
The singers lead the way, the players of strings follow,
and all around them young women beat their tambourines.
Bless God in the great assemblies;
bless the LORD, you who spring from Israel’s fountain.
There goes little Benjamin in the lead,
the princes of Judah in their crowded ranks,
then Zebulun’s princes and Naphtali’s princes.
Your God has decreed your strength, Israel.
Show your might, God,
as you have acted for us before.
On account of your temple high over Jerusalem,
kings will carry tribute to you.
Rebuke the beast that lurks among the reeds, that herd of bulls with the calves of the nations,
until they come bowing low with bars of silver.
God has scattered the peoples who love war.
High officials will come out of Egypt;
Cush will quickly lift its hands in prayer to God.
Sing to God, all you kingdoms on earth;
make music for the Lord. Selah
Sing to the one who rides across the ancient heavens, the heaven of heavens;
listen, he lets his voice ring out, his voice of power.
Declare that power belongs to God!
His majesty rests over Israel;
his might is in the clouds.
God, you inspire awe from your holy places;
Israel’s God is the one who gives his people strength and might.
Blessed be God!

fields.title: Psalm 69
fields.body_html:
Rescue me from the deep waters

For the music director. On shoshannim. Of David.

Rescue me, God,
for the water has risen to my throat.
I am sinking in deep mud with nothing to stand on;
I have gone down into deep water, and the current is carrying me away.
I am exhausted from calling out; my throat is burning dry.
My eyes have grown dim
from watching for my God.
There are more people hating me for no reason than hairs on my head;
strong are the ones who seek my ruin, my enemies with their lies.
Am I to repay what I never took?
God, you know my foolishness;
none of my guilt is hidden from you.
May no one who waits for you be shamed through me, Lord GOD of Armies;
may no one who seeks you be humiliated through me,
God of Israel.
Because of you I have carried scorn;
humiliation covers my face.
My own brothers treat me as a stranger;
to my mother’s sons I am an outsider.
Passion for your house burns me up,
and the taunts aimed at you have landed on me.
I wept and went without food,
and for that they mocked me.
When I put on sackcloth for clothing,
they made me the butt of their sayings.
The people who sit at the city gate gossip about me,
and drunkards sing songs mocking me.
But as for me, I pray to you, LORD, at a time you will accept;
God, in your great loyal love,
answer me with your faithful rescue.
Pull me out of the mud, and do not let me go under;
let me be snatched away from those who hate me, out of the deep water.
Do not let the flood waters wash over me or the deep gulp me down,
or the pit shut its mouth on me.
Answer me, LORD, because your loyal love is good;
in your great compassion, turn toward me.
Do not turn away from me, your servant;
I am hard pressed, so be quick to answer me.
Come close to me and buy me back;
set me free because of my enemies.
You know the scorn I bear, my shame and my disgrace;
every one of my enemies is in your sight.
Scorn has broken my heart, leaving me sick;
I hoped someone would pity me, but no one did,
that someone would comfort me, but there was no one to be found.
They put bitter poison into my food,
and for my thirst they handed me sour wine.
May the meal set before them become a trap for them,
a snare when they feel secure.
May their eyes grow dim until they cannot see;
make their bodies tremble without end.
Pour your fury out on them;
let your blazing anger catch up with them.
Let their camp become a wasteland,
with nobody living in their tents.
For they chase down the one you have struck,
and gossip about the pain of the people you have wounded.
Add guilt to their guilt;
let them have no share in your saving justice.
May their names be erased from the book of life,
never to be entered with the righteous.
But I am poor and hurting;
let your saving help, God, lift me up to safety.
With a song I will praise God’s name
and proclaim his greatness with thanksgiving.
That will delight the LORD more than an ox
or a young bull with full-grown horns and hooves.
The humble will see it and be glad;
you who seek God, take heart and live!
For the LORD hears the poor
and does not look down on his people in chains.
Let the heavens and the earth praise him,
the seas and all that swarms in them.
For God will rescue Zion and build up Judah’s towns again;
his people will live there and hold it as their own,
the descendants of his servants will receive it as their inheritance,
and all who love his name will make their home in it.

fields.title: Psalm 70
fields.body_html:
Hurry, God, and help me

For the music director. Of David. For remembrance.

God, come and rescue me!
LORD, be quick to help me!
Let those who are out to take my life be shamed and confounded;
let those who want me hurt be driven back in disgrace.
Let those who crow “Aha! Aha!”
retreat because of their own disgrace.
But may all who look for you be glad and take delight in you,
and let all who love your saving help keep saying, “God is great!”
As for me, I am poor and in need; God, come to me quickly!
You are my helper and the one who sets me free;
LORD, do not hold back!

fields.title: Psalm 71
fields.body_html:
Do not leave me now I am old

LORD, I have made you my refuge;
never let me be disgraced.
Because you are just, rescue me and set me free;
bend down to listen to me, and save me.
Be a rock I can live in, a place I can always come to.
You have given the order to save me,
since you yourself are my crag and my stronghold.
My God, pull me out of the clutches of the wicked,
out of the grip of the unjust and the cruel.
For you are my hope,
Lord GOD; I have trusted in you since I was young.
I have leaned on you from birth;
it was you who drew me from my mother’s body.
I will praise you without ceasing.
To many I have become a sign that makes them wonder,
but you are my strong shelter.
My mouth is full of praise for you;
all day long I speak of your glory.
Do not throw me aside now that I am old;
do not abandon me as my strength gives out.
For my enemies are talking about me;
those who are waiting to take my life are plotting together,
and they say, “God has abandoned him.
Go after him and grab him,
for no one will save him.”
God, do not stay far away from me;
my God, come quickly and help me!
Let my accusers be put to shame and brought to nothing;
let those who want to hurt me be wrapped in scorn and dishonor.
As for me, I will never stop hoping;
I will add to your praise again and again.
My mouth will tell of your righteousness
and of your saving help all day long,
though they are more than I can count.
I will come and tell of the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD;
I will call to mind your righteousness, yours and no one else’s.
God, you have been teaching me since I was young,
and I am telling of your wonders still.
Now that I am old and gray, God, do not abandon me,
not until I have told the generation after me what your arm has done,
and made your power known to all who are yet to be born.
God, your righteousness rises as high as the heavens;
you have done mighty things.
God, who is there like you?
You have made me see many troubles and hard times,
but you will bring me back to life,
and raise me once more out of the deep places of the earth.
Make me greater than before,
and turn to comfort me once more.
I in turn will thank you to the music of the harp; my God, I will praise your faithfulness.
With the lyre I will play for you,
Holy One of Israel.
My lips will ring out with joy as I sing your praise,
and so will my whole self, which you have set free.
All day long my tongue will speak of your righteousness,
for the people who sought my hurt are ashamed and humbled.

fields.title: Psalm 72
fields.body_html:
A prayer for the king’s reign

Of Solomon.

God, grant the king your justice,
and the king’s son your righteousness.
May he govern your people rightly,
and your poor with fairness.
May the mountains yield well-being for the people,
and the hills bring it through righteousness.
May he defend the poor among the people
and bring rescue to needy families;
may he break the oppressor in pieces.
May people stand in awe of you as long as there is a sun and a moon,
from one generation to the next.
May he be like rain falling on a cut field,
like showers soaking the land.
In his days may the righteous thrive,
and peace overflow until the moon is gone.
May his rule stretch from sea to sea,
from the River to the far ends of the earth.
Let the nomads of the desert kneel before him,
and let his foes lick the dust.
Let Tarshish and the coastlands send their kings with tribute;
let the kings of Sheba and Seba bring him presents.
Let every king bow low before him
and every nation be his servant.
For he rescues the needy when they cry out,
and the poor who have no one else to stand by them.
He feels for the weak and the needy,
and he saves the lives of those in need.
He sets them free from cruelty and violence;
their lives are of great worth in his sight.
May the king live! Let him receive Sheba’s gold;
let prayer be made for him always,
and blessing asked for him all day.
Let grain grow thick across the land, right up to the hilltops;
let its harvest rustle like the trees of Lebanon,
and let city people spring up like grass in the fields.
May his name live on forever,
his fame spread as long as the sun shines.
May all nations ask to be blessed as he is blessed, and call him happy.
Blessed be the LORD God, Israel’s God;
only he works wonders.
Blessed be his glorious name for all time;
may his glory fill all the earth.
Amen and Amen.
Here end the prayers of David son of Jesse.

fields.title: Psalm 73
fields.body_html:
Envy of the wicked, and nearness to God

A psalm of Asaph.

God really is good to Israel,
to people with a clean heart.
But I came close to losing my footing;
my steps very nearly slid out from under me.
I had grown jealous of the proud,
watching wicked people do well.
They die without pain,
and their bodies are plump and healthy.
They are free from the hardships others carry;
they are not plagued like the rest of humankind.
So they wear pride like a chain around the neck,
and violence wraps them like a robe.
Their eyes bulge from their fat faces;
the fancies of their minds run past all limits.
They jeer and talk of evil;
from on high they speak of crushing others.
Their mouths speak as if they owned heaven;
their tongues go swaggering through the land.
So his people turn their way
and gulp down their words like water from a full cup.
And they ask, “What can God know?
Is the Most High aware of anything?”
So these are the wicked:
never troubled, always growing richer.
So it was for nothing that I kept my heart clean
and washed my hands to show I was innocent.
I have been beaten down the whole day long,
and corrected afresh each morning.
Had I resolved to speak like this,
I would have broken faith with the family of your children.
So I tried to make sense of it,
but it seemed a weary task to me,
until I entered God’s holy place;
then I saw where they will end.
In fact, you have set them where the footing is slick,
and you let them crash into ruin.
In an instant they are ruined!
Sudden terrors make an end of them.
They are like a dream once the sleeper wakes;
Lord, when you stir, you will scorn them as mere shadows.
When my heart had turned sour
and I felt stabbed deep inside,
I was a fool and knew nothing;
in your presence I was no better than an animal.
Even so, I am with you at all times;
you have taken me by the right hand.
You lead me by your wise advice,
and at the end you will take me up in glory.
Who else is there for me in heaven?
And having you, I want nothing on earth.
Though body and heart wear out,
God is the rock my heart rests on and the share that is mine forever.
Those who move far from you are lost;
everyone who deserts you to love another, you cut off.
As for me, being close to God is my good;
in the Lord GOD I have found my shelter,
and I will tell of all you have done.

fields.title: Psalm 74
fields.body_html:
Remember your people and your ruined sanctuary

A maskil of Asaph.

God, why have you cast us off for good?
Why does your anger burn and smoke against the flock you tend?
Remember your people, whom you made your own long ago,
the tribe you bought back to be your inheritance;
remember Mount Zion, where you made your home.
Come, make your way over these ruins that never end;
the enemy has smashed everything in the holy place.
Your enemies roared in the middle of the place where you met with us;
they set up their own banners as signs.
They seemed like woodcutters lifting their axes
against a dense stand of trees.
And now they hack away at all its carved panels
with hatchets and hammers.
They set your sanctuary on fire;
they dragged the home of your name down to the ground and defiled it.
In their hearts they said, “Let us beat them down, all of them!”
They set fire to all God’s meeting places throughout the land.
We see no signs for us anymore;
no prophet is left,
and no one among us can say how long it will be.
How long, God, will the enemy jeer?
Will the foe go on insulting your name forever?
Why do you hold your hand still, your strong right hand?
Pull it out of your cloak and make an end of them!
But God has been my King since ancient times,
bringing rescue in the middle of the earth.
By your power you tore the sea in two;
you crushed the heads of the dragons in the water.
You shattered the heads of Leviathan
and gave it as food to the creatures of the desert.
You broke open springs and brooks;
you made rivers that always flowed run dry.
The day is yours, and the night is yours as well;
you set the moon and the sun in their places.
You fixed every boundary of the earth;
summer and winter are your handiwork.
Remember this, LORD: the enemy has jeered at you,
and a foolish people has insulted your name.
Do not let your dove fall prey to the greedy beasts;
do not leave your suffering people forgotten for good.
Pay heed to the covenant,
because every dark corner of the land is filled with places of violence.
Do not let the downtrodden go back ashamed;
may the poor and the needy give praise to your name.
Rise up, God! Take up your own case;
keep in mind the insults the fool throws at you all day long.
Do not ignore the shouting of your enemies,
the din of those who rise against you, which never stops rising.

fields.title: Psalm 75
fields.body_html:
God is judge: he lowers and lifts

For the music director. To the tune “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.

We thank you, God, we thank you; your name is close to us,
and people speak of the marvels you have done.
“When the time I have fixed has come,
I will judge with fairness.
The earth and everyone on it may sway and melt,
but I have set its pillars firm. Selah
I tell the proud, ‘Stop your boasting,’
and the wicked, ‘Do not toss your horn high.’
Do not raise your horn against the heights,
or talk with a stiff and insolent neck.”
For it is not from the east or the west,
nor from the desert, that a person is raised up,
but God is the judge:
he lays one person low and lifts another up.
For the LORD holds a cup in his hand, and the wine in it foams, richly spiced; he pours from it,
and every wicked person on earth will have to drain it, dregs and all.
But I will never stop telling of it;
I will make music to the God of Jacob.
I will hack off every horn the wicked raise,
but those who do right will have their horns lifted high.

fields.title: Psalm 76
fields.body_html:
God breaks the weapons at Zion

For the music director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.

God has made himself known in Judah;
his name stands high in Israel.
His lair is set in Salem,
his den in Zion.
There he shattered the fiery shafts of the bow,
shield and sword and all the gear of battle. Selah
You shine with light,
in greater splendor than the mountains of prey.
The brave were stripped bare; they dropped into their final sleep,
and not one of the warriors could find a hand to raise.
When you rebuked them, God of Jacob,
chariot and horse sank into a stupor.
You, yes, you are to be feared!
When your anger blazes,
who can hold out in your presence?
From heaven you announced your verdict;
the earth was afraid and fell silent,
when God stood up to give judgment
and to rescue all the lowly on earth. Selah
Even human fury will end in praise for you;
what is left of it you will tie on like a belt.
Vow to the LORD your God, and keep what you vow;
let all who surround him
bring tribute to the One who inspires fear.
He cuts short the breath of princes;
the kings of the earth stand in fear of him.

fields.title: Psalm 77
fields.body_html:
Remembering God’s way through the sea

For the music director. On Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph.

I raise my voice to God and cry out;
I raise my voice to God, so that he will listen to me.
When trouble came I looked for the Lord;
all night I kept my hands raised and did not tire,
and I would take no comfort.
I think of God and groan;
I ponder, and my spirit sinks. Selah
You would not let my eyelids close;
I was too shaken to say a word.
I turned my mind to days gone by,
to years long past.
I call to mind the songs I sang at night;
I talk with my own heart,
and my spirit searches for answers:
Will the Lord turn away for all time,
and never again show kindness?
Is his loyal love gone for good?
Is his promise finished for every generation to come?
Has God forgotten how to show mercy?
Has he let anger lock away his compassion? Selah
Then I said: This is what pierces me,
that the Most High’s right hand is not what it was.
I will call to mind what the LORD has done;
yes, I will remember the marvels you worked long ago.
I will reflect on all your work
and turn over in my mind what you have done.
God, your way is holy.
Is there a god anywhere as great as God?
You are the God whose deeds are marvels;
you have shown the nations how strong you are.
With your strong arm you set your people free,
the families of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
God, when the waters caught sight of you,
when the waters saw you, they twisted in fear;
even the deep sea quaked.
The clouds poured down rain,
the skies rumbled with thunder,
and your arrows flashed this way and that.
Your thunder rumbled in the whirlwind;
flashes of lightning lit the world;
the earth shook and quaked.
Your road went through the sea
and your track through the deep waters,
but no trace of your steps could be seen.
Like a shepherd with his sheep you guided your people,
through Moses and Aaron.

fields.title: Psalm 78
fields.body_html:
Tell the next generation: grace despite rebellion

A maskil of Asaph.

My people, listen closely to my instruction;
bend your ears to what I say.
I will open my mouth to speak a parable;
I will bring out the hidden lessons of long ago,
what we have heard and learned,
what our forebears passed on to us.
We will not conceal them from their children;
we will pass on to those who come after us the deeds for which the LORD is praised,
his strength, and the marvels he has worked.
He laid down a solemn charge in Jacob and set up instruction in Israel;
he ordered our forebears
to teach these to their children,
so that those born later, children not yet born, would know them,
and would grow up and tell them to their own children,
so that they would rest their hope on God,
remember the works of God,
and keep his commands,
and would not be like their ancestors, a defiant and rebellious generation,
whose hearts were never steady
and whose spirits did not stay true to God.
The Ephraimites, armed and skilled with the bow,
fled when the day of battle came.
They failed to keep the covenant God had made
and would not follow his instruction.
They let his deeds slip from memory,
the marvels they had seen him work.
In full view of their ancestors he worked marvels
in Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
He split the sea in two and took them across,
piling up the waters in a heap.
By day he guided them with the cloud,
and all through the night with the glow of fire.
He broke open rocks in the desert
and let them drink water as plentiful as the ocean depths.
He drew streams out of the cliff
and sent water rushing down like rivers.
Yet they kept on sinning against him,
defying the Most High in the parched desert.
In their hearts they challenged God,
insisting on food to feed their cravings.
They spoke against God
and said, “Can God lay out a meal in the desert?
Yes, he hit the rock and water burst out and torrents swept along;
but is he able to give bread too,
or to put meat before his people?”
So when the LORD heard it, he was enraged;
fire blazed up against Jacob,
and his anger rose against Israel,
because they had no faith in God
and did not rely on his power to save.
Even so, he gave orders to the clouds above
and threw open the doors of the sky,
and showered manna on them for food;
he handed them grain from heaven.
Everyone ate the bread of the mighty ones;
he sent them supplies until they had their fill.
He set the east wind moving across the sky
and steered the south wind by his power.
He showered meat on them as thick as dust,
birds on the wing as many as the grains of sand by the sea.
He brought them down in the middle of their camp,
all around their tents.
They ate and were more than satisfied;
he gave them what they longed for.
They had not yet turned away from their craving;
they were still chewing their food,
when the anger of God blazed against them;
he slew the best-fed among them
and brought down the young men of Israel.
Even so they went on sinning;
in spite of his marvels they would not believe.
So he let their days drift away like vapor
and ended their years in sudden dread.
Whenever he struck them down, they would look for him;
they would turn back and search hard for God.
They recalled that their Rock was God,
that God Most High was the one who had set them free.
But their words to him were only flattery;
with their tongues they lied to him,
and their hearts were not set on him;
they did not stay true to his covenant.
Yet he was full of compassion; he covered their guilt and did not wipe them out.
Many a time he held back his anger
and did not let all his fury loose.
He remembered that they were only flesh,
a breeze that blows past and does not come back.
How many times they defied him in the wilderness
and caused him grief in the barren land!
Once more they challenged God
and wounded the Holy One of Israel.
They forgot his power
and the day he bought them free from the enemy,
when he displayed his signs in Egypt
and his marvels in the fields around Zoan.
He changed their rivers into blood,
and their running water could not be drunk.
He sent swarms of insects among them to eat them up,
and frogs to bring them to ruin.
He handed their harvest over to the grasshopper
and all they had worked for to the swarming locust.
He struck their vines dead with hail
and froze their sycamore-figs with ice.
He left their cattle at the mercy of the hail,
and their herds to the flashing fire.
He let loose on them the heat of his anger,
rage and fury and distress,
a troop of angels bringing disaster.
He cleared a road for his anger;
he did not hold them back from death,
but handed their lives over to the plague.
He cut down every firstborn in Egypt,
the eldest sons, the first of their strength, throughout the tents of Ham.
Then he moved his people out like sheep
and herded them like a flock across the wilderness.
He kept them safe as he led them, and they were not afraid;
but the sea closed over their enemies.
He led them to his sacred land,
to these mountains that his own power had gained.
He pushed out nations ahead of them
and shared out their land by measuring line as a possession;
he gave the tribes of Israel their tents to live in.
Still they challenged God Most High and defied him;
they did not keep his decrees.
They turned away and broke faith as their ancestors did;
they went crooked like a warped bow.
They angered him with their hilltop shrines,
and by their idols roused his jealous anger.
When God heard, his anger blazed,
and he cast Israel off entirely.
He deserted the sanctuary at Shiloh,
the tent where he had made his home among people.
He let his might be carried off as a captive,
his glory into enemy hands.
He handed his people over to the sword;
he raged against his own inheritance.
Their young men were eaten up by fire;
no one sang the wedding song for their young women.
Their priests were cut down by the sword,
and the widows they left could not raise a lament.
Then the Lord roused himself like a sleeper waking,
like a warrior shouting as the wine stirs him.
He beat his enemies back
and put them to lasting shame.
He turned down the tent of Joseph;
Ephraim’s tribe was not the one he chose,
instead he picked out the tribe of Judah
and Mount Zion, which he holds dear.
He made his sanctuary as lofty as the heavens
and as firm as the earth, which he founded to last forever.
He singled out David, his servant,
and called him away from the sheepfolds,
from walking behind the nursing ewes he brought him
to care for Jacob, his people,
and for Israel, his own possession, as their shepherd.
He cared for them as a shepherd with an honest heart
and led them with skillful hands.

fields.title: Psalm 79
fields.body_html:
A plea for ruined Jerusalem

A psalm of Asaph.

God, the nations have broken into the land that is your own;
they have made your holy temple unclean
and turned Jerusalem into piles of rubble.
They have thrown out the bodies of your servants for the birds of the air to eat,
and the flesh of your faithful people for the wild animals.
They have spilled their blood like water on every side of Jerusalem,
and no one was left to bury them.
We have become a disgrace in our neighbors’ eyes,
laughed at and scorned by everyone near us.
How long, LORD? Will you be angry without end?
Must your jealousy keep burning like fire?
Pour out your fury on the nations that have not known you,
on the kingdoms
that never call on your name,
for they have swallowed up Jacob
and left his homeland desolate.
Do not count against us the wrongs of those who came before us;
let your compassion hurry to meet us,
for we are at the end of our strength.
God who saves us, come to our help for the glory of your name.
Rescue us and cover our sins, to honor your name.
Why should the nations get to say, “Where is their God?”
Let the nations see you pay back the blood of your servants that was shed,
and let us see it with our own eyes.
May the groaning of the captives reach you;
with the might of your arm,
spare those who are marked for death.
Pay back our neighbors seven times over, right into their laps,
for the scorn they have heaped on you, Lord.
Then we, your people, the flock you tend, will thank you for all time;
to every generation
we will tell of your praise.

fields.title: Psalm 80
fields.body_html:
Restore your vine, God of Armies

For the music director. On shoshannim eduth. Of Asaph. A psalm.

Turn your ear to us, Shepherd of Israel,
guiding Joseph like a flock!
Throned above the cherubim, blaze out in splendor!
Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh,
rouse your strength
and come to rescue us!
God, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.
LORD God of Armies,
how long will you seethe with anger even while your people pray?
You have made tears their food,
and given them full measures of tears to drink.
You make us something our neighbors fight over,
and our enemies sneer at us among themselves.
God of Armies, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.
You lifted a vine out of Egypt;
you expelled nations to plant it.
You prepared the soil to receive it;
it put down its roots and covered the land.
Its shadow spread over the mountains,
and its branches over the giant cedars.
It stretched its branches as far as the sea,
and its shoots to the River.
Why did you break down the walls around it?
Now everyone who walks along the road picks its grapes.
Wild boars from the forest tear it up,
and the creatures of the open country feed on it.
God of Armies, please come back!
Gaze down from heaven and see;
care for this vine,
the root your right hand planted,
the son you raised to strength for yourself.
It has been burned with fire and cut down;
your people are dying under your angry rebuke.
Let your hand protect the man at your right hand,
the son of man you raised to strength for yourself.
Then we will not drift away from you.
Bring us back to life, and we will call on you by name.
LORD God of Armies, bring us back!
Turn the light of your face on us, and we will be saved.

fields.title: Psalm 81
fields.body_html:
If only my people would listen

For the music director. On the gittith. Of Asaph.

Sing out with joy to God, our strength;
raise a shout to the God of Jacob!
Strike up the music and beat the tambourine;
play the sweet lyre along with the harp.
At the new moon, blow the ram’s horn,
and at the full moon, for our feast day,
for this is a law laid down for Israel,
a rule given by the God of Jacob.
He made it a solemn charge for Joseph
when he went out against the land of Egypt.
Then I heard a voice I had never known:
“I lifted the heavy load from their shoulders;
their hands let go of the brick basket.
When you were in trouble you cried out, and I set you free;
I answered you from the hidden place of the thunder;
I put you to the test at the waters of Meribah. Selah
Listen, my people, and I will give you a solemn warning;
Israel, oh, that you would listen to me!
You must have no strange god among you;
you must not bow down to any foreign god.
I am the LORD your God,
the one who led you up out of Egypt’s land.
Open your mouth as wide as you can, and I will fill it.
But my people refused to listen to my voice;
Israel would have nothing to do with me.
So I left them to their stubborn hearts,
and they followed their own schemes.
If only my people were listening to me,
if only Israel would walk in my paths,
I would soon bring their enemies low
and turn my hand against their attackers.
Those who hate the LORD would come cringing to him,
and their doom would never end.
He would give them the finest wheat to eat,
and I would fill you up with honey from the rock.”

fields.title: Psalm 82
fields.body_html:
God judges the gods

A psalm of Asaph.

God takes his stand in the divine assembly;
he gives judgment among the gods.
“How long will you judge unfairly
and take the side of the wicked? Selah
Judge fairly for the weak and for orphans;
declare the afflicted and the destitute in the right.
Bring the weak and the poor to safety;
snatch them from the grip of the wicked.
They have no knowledge and no understanding;
they wander around in the dark,
and the earth’s foundations all totter.
I myself said, ‘You are gods;
every one of you is a son of the Most High.’
Yet you will die as human beings die,
and fall like any one of the princes.”
Rise up, God, judge the earth,
since every nation belongs to you.

fields.title: Psalm 83
fields.body_html:
Do not keep silent, God

A song. A psalm of Asaph.

God, do not rest!
Do not keep silent, and do not sit idle, God!
Look, your enemies are in an uproar;
those who hate you hold their heads high.
They are plotting slyly against your people
and conspiring against those you treasure.
They say, “Come, let us wipe them out so they are no longer a nation;
let no one ever again remember the name of Israel.”
They have agreed together with one mind;
they are making a treaty against you,
Edom’s tent-dwellers, the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia and the people who live in Tyre.
Assyria too has joined them;
they lend their strength to the descendants of Lot. Selah
Treat them the way you treated Midian,
the way you treated Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon valley,
who were wiped out at Endor
and became manure on the ground.
Deal with their nobles as with Oreb and Zeeb,
and with all their chiefs as with Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said,
“Let us take God’s pasturelands as our own.”
My God, make them like a tumbleweed spinning away,
like husks driven by the wind.
As a fire eats through a forest,
as flames set the mountainsides alight,
so hunt them down with your storm
and fill them with terror by your gale.
Load their faces with disgrace,
so that they come seeking your name, LORD.
May they be shamed and terrified for all time;
may they be disgraced and come to ruin,
and let them come to know that your name is the LORD,
that only you are Most High over the whole earth.

fields.title: Psalm 84
fields.body_html:
Longing for the LORD’s house

For the music director. On the gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.

How deeply loved is your dwelling place,
LORD of Armies!
My whole being longs, even aches, for the courts of the LORD;
heart and body,
I shout with joy to the living God.
The sparrow, too, has found itself a home, and the swallow has a nest where it keeps its young,
beside your altars, LORD of Armies,
my King and my God.
How blessed are the ones who live in your house;
they never stop praising you. Selah
How blessed are people who find their strength in you
