I am waiting for the LORD; with all that I am I wait, and I hope in what he has promised.
I long for the Lord more than night guards long for the morning, yes, more than night guards for the morning.
Israel, wait in hope for the LORD! For loyal love is found with the LORD, and with him is redemption in full measure.
It is he who will redeem Israel from all its wrongs.

fields.title: Psalm 131
fields.body_html:
Calm like a weaned child

A song of ascents. Of David.

LORD, there is no pride in my heart, no arrogance in my eyes. I do not go after things too great for me, or too wonderful for me to grasp.
Instead, I have made myself calm and quiet, like a child past nursing age resting on its mother; I am calm within, like that child.
Israel, wait in hope for the LORD, from now on and forever.

fields.title: Psalm 132
fields.body_html:
The LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion

A song of ascents.

LORD, remember David and all the hardship he went through,
how he made an oath to the LORD and a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob,
“I will not set foot in my own house or climb into my bed,
I will not let my eyes sleep or my eyelids close,
until I have found the LORD a place to stay, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
Listen! We heard of it in Ephrathah, and came across it in the fields of Jaar.
Come, we will enter his home and bow down before the footstool under his feet.
Rise up, LORD! Come to the place where you will rest, you and the ark of your might.
Let your priests be dressed in righteousness, and let those loyal to you cry out with joy.
Because of David your servant, do not refuse the king you have anointed.
The LORD has given David his word on oath, a true word he will never take back: “I will place a child of your own body on your throne.
If your sons are faithful to my covenant and to the decrees I will teach them, their sons as well will sit on your throne for all time.”
For the LORD chose Zion; he longed to make it his home.
“Here is my resting place for all time; I will live here, for this is the place I longed for.
I will richly bless the city’s food supply; I will give its poor all the bread they need.
I will dress its priests in salvation, and its faithful people will shout and sing for joy.
There I will make David’s horn sprout up; I have trimmed a lamp for my anointed king.
I will dress his enemies in shame, but the crown on his head will gleam.”

fields.title: Psalm 133
fields.body_html:
How good it is to live as one

A song of ascents. Of David.

See how good it is, how lovely, when brothers and sisters live together in harmony!
It is like the fine anointing oil on the head that flows down the beard, down Aaron’s beard, and down over the collar of his robes,
like the dew of Hermon coming down on the hills of Zion. For it is there that the LORD has decreed the blessing, life without end.

fields.title: Psalm 134
fields.body_html:
Bless the LORD by night

A song of ascents.

Now bless the LORD, every servant of the LORD who stands night after night in the house of the LORD!
Raise your hands toward the sanctuary, and bless the LORD!
From Zion may the LORD, the one who made heaven and earth, bless you.

fields.title: Psalm 135
fields.body_html:
Praise the LORD, who chose Israel

Praise the LORD! Praise the name of the LORD; give him praise, you servants of the LORD,
who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courtyards of the house of our God.
Praise the LORD, for the LORD is good; make music to his name, for that is a delight.
For the LORD chose Jacob to be his own, Israel to be his special treasure.
I am sure of it: the LORD is great, and our Lord stands above all gods.
Whatever the LORD chooses to do, he does it, in the heavens, on the earth, in the seas and in all the ocean depths.
He raises the clouds from the far edges of the earth; he makes lightning flash with the rain and brings the wind out of his storehouses.
He struck down the firstborn of Egypt, of people and of animals alike.
Into your very heart, Egypt, he sent signs and wonders, against Pharaoh and all his officials.
He struck down many nations and killed powerful kings,
Sihon king of the Amorites, Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan,
and he gave their land away as a heritage, a heritage for his people Israel.
LORD, your name will last forever; LORD, people will remember you in every generation.
For the LORD will take up the cause of his people and show pity to his servants.
The idols of the nations are made of silver and gold, shaped by human hands.
They have a mouth, yet say nothing; they have eyes, yet see nothing.
They have ears, yet hear nothing; there is not even breath in their mouths.
The people who make them will end up like them, and so will everyone who relies on them.
People of Israel, bless the LORD! Family of Aaron, bless the LORD!
Family of Levi, bless the LORD! All who fear the LORD, bless the LORD!
May the LORD be blessed from Zion, he who lives in Jerusalem. Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Psalm 136
fields.body_html:
His loyal love lasts forever

Give the LORD thanks, for he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of gods, for his loyal love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who alone does great wonders, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who made the heavens with skill and wisdom, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who spread out the land over the waters, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who made the great lights, for his loyal love lasts forever.
the sun to rule by day, for his loyal love lasts forever.
the moon and the stars to rule by night, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who struck Egypt through their firstborn, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he led Israel out from among them, for his loyal love lasts forever.
with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who split the Red Sea apart, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he brought Israel through the middle of it, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he shook Pharaoh and his army off into the Red Sea, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who guided his people through the wilderness, for his loyal love lasts forever.
To the one who struck down great kings, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he killed powerful kings, for his loyal love lasts forever.
Sihon king of the Amorites, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and Og king of Bashan, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he gave their land away as a heritage, for his loyal love lasts forever.
a heritage for Israel his servant, for his loyal love lasts forever.
who remembered us when we were brought low, for his loyal love lasts forever.
and he tore us free from our enemies, for his loyal love lasts forever.
who gives food to every living creature, for his loyal love lasts forever.
Give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loyal love lasts forever.

fields.title: Psalm 137
fields.body_html:
By the rivers of Babylon

Beside the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down; we wept as we thought of Zion.
On the poplar trees there we hung up our lyres.
For there the people who had taken us captive demanded songs from us; those who tormented us wanted us to be cheerful: “Sing for us a song from Zion!”
How could we sing the LORD’s song in a land of strangers?
Jerusalem, if I ever forget you, may my right hand forget how to play.
May my tongue stay stuck to the roof of my mouth should I fail to remember you, should I fail to prize Jerusalem above my chief delight.
LORD, hold the day of Jerusalem’s fall against the Edomites, who shouted, “Strip it, strip it bare, right down to its foundations!”
Daughter Babylon, soon to be laid waste, how blessed is the one who pays you back in full for all you did to us!
How blessed is the one who grabs your little children and smashes them on the rock!

fields.title: Psalm 138
fields.body_html:
Thanks for an answered prayer

Of David.

With all my heart I will give you thanks; in the presence of the gods I will make music for you.
I will bow down facing your holy temple and praise your name for your loyal love and your faithfulness; for you have made your promise great, beyond all that your name had made known.
The day I called, you answered me; you filled me with courage and strength within.
LORD, every king on earth will give you thanks, because they have heard the words you spoke.
They will sing of the LORD’s ways, because the glory of the LORD is so great.
The LORD is high, yet he looks upon those who are low; the proud he knows from a distance.
Even when I walk through the middle of trouble, you keep me alive. You reach out your hand against my enemies’ fury, and your right hand rescues me.
The LORD will carry out his plan for me. LORD, your loyal love lasts forever; do not let go of what your hands have made.

fields.title: Psalm 139
fields.body_html:
The LORD knows me through and through

For the music director. Of David. A psalm.

LORD, you have looked deep into me, and you know me.
Whether I sit down or get up, you know it;
even from far away you grasp what I am thinking.
When I travel and when I lie down, you sift through it all;
every path I take is well known to you.
No word is yet on my tongue,
and already, LORD, you know the whole of it.
You close me in from behind and from in front;
you have placed your hand on me.
Knowledge like this is beyond me, too wonderful;
it towers so high that I cannot reach it.
Where could I go to get away from your Spirit?
Where could I run to escape your presence?
Should I climb up to the heavens, you are there;
should I lie down in Sheol, there you are as well.
If I take flight on the wings of the dawn
and go to live beyond the farthest sea,
there too your hand would be leading me,
and your right hand would take hold of me.
If I tell myself that the darkness will surely overwhelm me
and the light around me will turn to night,
even the darkness hides nothing from you;
night shines as bright as day,
and dark and light are the same to you.
It was you who made the deepest parts of me;
you wove my body together while I was still in my mother’s womb.
I give you thanks, for the way I was made is awe-inspiring and marvelous.
What you make is wonderful,
and deep within I know it well.
Not one of my bones was hidden from you
as I was being formed out of sight,
worked like fine embroidery deep within the earth.
Your eyes saw me while I was still unshaped; in your book they were all written down,
the days that were shaped for me,
each one of them set in place.
God, how I treasure your thoughts!
How immense their number is!
Should I try to count them, they would outnumber the sand.
I wake up, and I am with you still.
God, if only you would put the wicked to death!
Murderers, get away from me,
those who name you as they plot their wickedness;
your enemies speak your name in falsehood.
LORD, how could I not hate those who hate you,
or feel disgust for those who rise up against you?
My hatred for them is total;
they have become my own enemies.
God, look deep into me and know my heart;
put me to the test and know my restless thoughts.
Look and see whether I am on a path that brings harm,
and guide me along the road that never ends.

fields.title: Psalm 140
fields.body_html:
Rescue me from violent people

For the music director. A psalm of David.

LORD, rescue me from evil people; keep me safe from those who do violence,
who scheme harm in their hearts and keep starting battles day after day.
They whet their tongues like a serpent; viper’s venom lies hidden behind their lips. Selah
LORD, guard me from the clutches of the wicked; shield me from violent people who are scheming to make me fall.
Arrogant people have hidden a trap for me; they have stretched out ropes as a net beside the path and laid snares to catch me. Selah
I have told the LORD, “You are my God.” Turn your ear, LORD, to the sound of my pleading.
Lord GOD, mighty one who saves me, you have covered my head on the day the weapons clash.
LORD, do not give the wicked what they crave; do not let their scheme succeed, or they will grow proud. Selah
As for those who close in around me, may the harm their own lips speak come down over their heads.
Let burning coals rain down on them; may they be hurled into fire, into deep pits, never to get up again.
Let no slanderer find a firm place in the land; let disaster hunt down the violent and strike them again and again.
I know that the LORD will take up the case of the oppressed and see that the needy get justice.
The righteous will surely give thanks to your name, and people of integrity will make their home before you.

fields.title: Psalm 141
fields.body_html:
A guard over my mouth

A psalm of David.

LORD, I am calling to you; come to me quickly. Hear my voice as I cry out to you.
Let my prayer stand before you like incense, my lifted hands like the offering at evening.
LORD, station a guard at my mouth; keep a sentry at the doorway of my lips.
Keep my heart from leaning toward anything evil, from joining with wrongdoers in their wicked acts; let me not share their rich food.
Let a righteous person strike me: that is loyal love. Let them reprove me: that is oil for my head, and may my head never refuse it. But all the while I pray against the evil they do.
When their rulers are flung down the face of the cliff, people will hear my words and know that they were kind.
Like clods when the ground is plowed and broken open, our bones lie scattered at the mouth of Sheol.
But my eyes look to you, Lord GOD; I make you my refuge. Do not let my life be poured out.
Guard me from the grip of the trap they have set for me, from the snares of those who do wrong.
May the wicked be caught together in their own nets, while I make my way past.

fields.title: Psalm 142
fields.body_html:
A prayer from the cave

A maskil of David, when he was in the cave. A prayer.

I call out loud to the LORD; I raise my voice to the LORD, pleading for mercy.
I spill out my complaint in front of him; I tell him all about my distress.
When my spirit is fading within me, you are the one who knows my path. Along the road I travel they have hidden a trap for me.
Look to my right and see: there is no one who knows me. Every way of escape is gone; nobody looks out for me.
I cry out to you, LORD. I say, “You are my shelter, all I have in the land of the living.”
Pay heed to my cry, because I am in the depths. Rescue me from those who hunt me, since they are stronger than I am.
Lead me out of this prison, so that I may thank your name. Then the righteous will crowd around me, because you will treat me with goodness.

fields.title: Psalm 143
fields.body_html:
Do not bring your servant to trial

A psalm of David.

LORD, hear my prayer; listen as I plead for mercy. Answer me in your faithfulness and in your righteousness.
Do not bring your servant to trial, for no living person can be found in the right before you.
The enemy has hunted me down and ground my life into the dust; he has left me to live in dark places, like people dead for ages.
My spirit sinks within me, and my heart is stunned inside me.
I recall the days long past; I think over all that you have done and reflect on what your hands have made.
I hold out my hands to you; my whole being waits for you like ground worn out by drought. Selah
LORD, hurry and answer me; my spirit is failing. Do not keep your face hidden from me, or I will become one of those who sink into the pit.
Each morning let me hear of your loyal love, since you are the one I rely on. Teach me which road to walk, for my whole being reaches up to you.
Snatch me from my enemies, LORD; I have taken cover with you.
Teach me to do what pleases you, since you are my God. May your Spirit, who is good, guide me across even ground.
LORD, for the honor of your name, keep me alive; in your righteousness lead me out of my distress.
In your loyal love you will put an end to my enemies and wipe out all who attack my life, for I am your servant.

fields.title: Psalm 144
fields.body_html:
A prayer for the king’s victory

Of David.

Blessed be the LORD, my rock, the one who teaches my hands to fight and my fingers to make war.
He is my loyal love and my stronghold, my tower on the heights and the one who sets me free, my shield, the one I shelter in, who brings my people under my rule.
LORD, what are human beings, that you take notice of them, mere mortals, that you give them a thought?
Human beings are like a breath; their days are a shadow sliding by.
LORD, bow your heavens low and come down; touch the mountains and make them pour out smoke.
Make the lightning flash and scatter the enemy; let your arrows fly and throw them into confusion.
Reach out your hands from on high; free me and pull me out of deep waters, out of the grip of foreigners,
who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
God, I will sing you a new song; I will play music for you on the ten-stringed harp,
the one who gives victory to kings, who snatches his servant David away from the cruel sword.
Free me and pull me out of the grip of foreigners, who speak nothing but lies with their mouths, and whose right hand is raised to swear what is false.
Then may our sons be like saplings grown tall while they are still young, and our daughters like corner columns carved for a royal house,
our storehouses full, supplying every kind of food, our flocks multiplying into the thousands, tens of thousands across our pastures,
our cattle heavy with young. May there be no breach in our walls, no going out into exile, no cry of distress in our streets.
How blessed the people who live like this! How blessed the people who have the LORD as their God!

fields.title: Psalm 145
fields.body_html:
My God the King, forever praised

A song of praise. Of David.

My God, the King, I will lift you high in praise and bless your name for ever and ever.
Day after day I will bless you and give praise to your name for ever and ever.
The LORD is great, worthy of the highest praise, and there is no searching out the depth of his greatness.
Each generation will praise your works to the one after it and announce your mighty acts.
I will reflect on your majesty, its glory and splendor, and on the story of your wonders.
People will speak of the power of your fearsome deeds, and I will tell of your greatness.
They will spill over with the memory of your great goodness and sing out for joy at your righteousness.
The LORD is full of grace and compassion, slow to anger and great in loyal love.
The LORD is good to everyone; his compassion covers all that he has made.
LORD, all your works will thank you, and your faithful people will bless you.
They will speak of your glorious reign and tell of your power,
to make his mighty acts known to all people, and the glorious splendor of his reign.
Your kingdom is a kingdom for all the ages, and your rule lasts through every generation.
The LORD holds up everyone who stumbles and raises all who are bent low.
All eyes are turned to you in hope, and you provide their food when it is needed.
You open your hand and give every living creature what it longs for.
In all his ways the LORD is righteous; in all his deeds he is faithful.
The LORD is close to everyone who calls to him, to all who call to him sincerely.
He grants what those who fear him desire; he hears their cry for help and rescues them.
The LORD guards everyone who loves him, but he will wipe out all the wicked.
With my own mouth I will speak praise to the LORD; may all creatures bless his holy name for all time to come.

fields.title: Psalm 146
fields.body_html:
Trust the God of Jacob, not rulers

Praise the LORD! My soul, praise the LORD!
All my life I will praise the LORD; as long as I exist I will make music for my God.
Do not rely on rulers, on mere mortals, who have no power to rescue.
Their breath leaves them and they go back to the soil they came from; that same day all they had planned is gone.
How blessed are those who have the God of Jacob to help them, whose hope rests on the LORD their God!
who made heaven and earth and the sea with all they contain, who remains true forever,
who brings justice to the oppressed and provides bread for the hungry. The LORD releases the prisoners;
The LORD makes the blind see; the LORD raises up those bent low; the LORD loves people who are righteous;
The LORD protects the foreigners living in the land; he upholds the orphan and the widow, but he overturns the way of the wicked.
The LORD will rule as King forever; Zion, your God will reign from one generation to the next. Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Psalm 147
fields.body_html:
The LORD who counts stars and heals

Praise the LORD! It is good to make music for our God; it is a delight, and praise is fitting.
The LORD is rebuilding Jerusalem; he is bringing together Israel’s scattered exiles.
He heals those whose hearts are crushed and bandages their injuries.
He decides how many stars there are and gives each one its name.
Our Lord is great and mighty in power; there is no measuring his understanding.
The LORD lifts up the lowly and throws the wicked down to the earth.
Sing out to the LORD with thanks; make music for our God on the lyre,
who wraps the sky in clouds, who gets rain ready for the land, who makes grass sprout on the mountains,
who gives the beasts their food and feeds the raven’s chicks when they call.
It is not the power of the horse that delights him, nor a soldier’s strong legs that please him.
What pleases the LORD is people who revere him and look with hope to his loyal love.
Jerusalem, glorify the LORD! Zion, praise your God!
For he has made the bars of your gates strong and has blessed your children inside your walls.
He keeps your frontiers at peace and satisfies you with the richest wheat.
He issues his orders to the earth, and his word goes out at a run.
He sends snow that lies like wool and strews frost like ash.
He flings down his ice in pieces like crumbs; who can hold out against his cold?
He sends his word, and the ice thaws; he sets his wind blowing, and the waters run.
He makes his words known to Jacob, his statutes and his rulings to Israel.
No other nation has he treated this way; his rulings are unknown to them. Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Psalm 148
fields.body_html:
All creation, praise the LORD

Praise the LORD! Let the heavens praise the LORD; let the heights above give him praise!
Praise him, all his angels! All the armies of heaven, praise him!
Sun and moon, praise him! All shining stars, praise him!
Praise him, heaven of heavens, along with the waters up above the sky!
May they praise the name of the LORD; at his command they came into being.
He fixed them in their places for ever and always; he made a law for them that will not pass away.
From the earth below, praise the LORD, sea monsters and all the watery deeps,
fire and hail, snow and fog, gales of wind that do what he says,
the mountains and all the hills, trees that bear fruit and all the cedars,
wild beasts and all cattle, creatures that crawl and birds that fly,
earthly kings and all peoples, nobles and all the earth’s rulers,
young men and young women alike, the old together with the young!
Let them all bring praise to the name of the LORD, since his name alone is lifted high; his splendor towers over earth and sky.
For his own people he has raised up a horn, a source of praise for all his faithful, the Israelites, a people near to him. Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Psalm 149
fields.body_html:
A new song for the faithful

Praise the LORD! Sing a new song to the LORD; sing his praise where the faithful gather!
Let Israel be glad in the one who made it; let Zion’s people rejoice in their King.
Let them praise his name in dance and make music for him on tambourine and lyre.
For the LORD is pleased with his people; he dresses the humble in the beauty of salvation.
Let the faithful be jubilant in their glory; let them cry out with joy as they lie on their beds.
with songs that lift God high in their throats and a two-edged sword held in their hands,
to bring retribution on the nations and to punish the peoples,
to put their kings in chains and their nobles in iron shackles,
to carry out on them the judgment already written. This honor belongs to all his faithful. Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Psalm 150
fields.body_html:
Everything that breathes, praise him

Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place; praise him in the great expanse of his power!
Praise him for the mighty things he has done; praise him as fits his boundless greatness!
Praise him with the ram’s horn blast; praise him with harp and lyre!
Praise him with hand drum and dance; praise him on strings and pipes!
Praise him with clear-sounding cymbals; praise him with cymbals that ring out like a shout!
Let every creature that breathes praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
Praise the LORD! Praise God in his holy place; praise him in the great expanse of his power!

— Psalm 150:1

The Psalms begin with a single person on a path, delighting in God’s instruction. They end with everything that breathes, praising. In between lies the whole of human life: enemies and exile, sin and forgiveness, sickness and long nights, festivals and harvests, kings who rose and kings who fell. The book has never once looked away from trouble. And yet it ends here.

Psalm 150 is the shortest possible summary of everything the Psalter has learned. It gives no new reason for praise; the hundred and forty-nine psalms before it have given them all. It says only where God is to be praised (in his holy place, and in the great expanse of his power), why (“for the mighty things he has done”), how (with the ram’s horn, harp and lyre, hand drum and dance, strings and pipes, and cymbals that ring out like a shout) and who. The answer to that last question is the book’s last line, and it leaves no one out.

Where the Psalms point

The ending is not a mood. The psalmists who wrote “How long, LORD?” did not stop meaning it when they wrote “Praise the LORD!” The book ends in praise because it believes that is where history ends: with the LORD as King over all the earth, the nations gathered to him, and his loyal love proved true. Again and again the Psalms look forward to that day, and their hope was larger than anything Israel had yet seen.

Christians read that hope as fulfilled in Jesus. He is the blessed one of Psalm 1 who delighted in God’s law, and the son of Psalm 2 whom the nations raged against. He prayed Psalm 22 on the cross, and its second half, the praise in the great assembly and the ends of the earth turning to the LORD, began to come true when he rose. He is the lord of Psalm 110, seated at God’s right hand; the shepherd of Psalm 23, who said, “I am the good shepherd”; the stone the builders cast aside. And the church has never stopped singing the Psalms, from the first Christians who were urged to speak to one another in “psalms, hymns and Spirit-given songs” to every congregation and every lonely reader who has prayed them since.

So the call of Psalm 150 is not only to the choirs of the temple. It reaches the reader of this book, wherever the Psalms have found you: in a lament, in a confession, on a pilgrimage, or already singing.

Where to go from here

Preachers and writers have lived in the Psalms for as long as there has been a church, and many of the best of them are in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On the shepherd psalm (Psalm 23). Alexander Maclaren’s The Shepherd King of Israel reads it as the old king David looking back on his shepherd years; Hudson Taylor’s Blessed Adversity takes up its last verse.
  • On the two paths (Psalm 1). Hudson Taylor’s Blessed Prosperity.
  • On longing and lament. Maclaren’s Thirsting for God (Psalm 42), Spurgeon’s Waiting Only Upon God (Psalm 62) and Elisabeth Elliot’s I Keep a Quiet Heart (Psalm 131).
  • On God our refuge (Psalms 46 and 91). A. W. Tozer’s God Is Our Refuge and Strength, and Maclaren’s The City and River of God and The Sheltering Wing.
  • On pilgrimage (Psalms 84 and 121). Elisabeth Elliot’s Hearts Set on Pilgrimage, A. B. Simpson’s From Strength to Strength and Maclaren’s Looking to the Hills.
  • On the cross (Psalms 22 and 31). Maclaren’s Into Thy Hands and Robert Murray M’Cheyne’s The Spirit Committed to God, both on the prayer Jesus prayed as he died; Justin Martyr’s Dialogue with Trypho, for how the earliest Christians read Psalm 22 and Psalm 110.
  • On praise. Maclaren’s The Satisfier of All Desires (Psalm 145), and on Psalm 147, Spurgeon’s Healing for the Wounded and Tozer’s The Infinite God.
  • On praying and singing the Psalms. William Law’s A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life, with its chapter on chanting psalms in private devotion; Andrew Murray’s The Inner Chamber, on Psalm 119; Hannah Whitall Smith’s The Christian’s Secret of a Happy Life, on Psalm 139; and The Prayers Jesus Learned, an Ochorus Original on the prayers of the Old Testament, David’s psalms among them.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to the Psalms in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, psalm by psalm, what the great writers of the church have said about each one.

But the best next step may simply be to keep reading the Psalms, one a day or five, and to pray them as you go. They were never meant to be finished. Readers who have prayed them all their lives say they understand them better each time, because each time they bring more of their own life to them. The book is waiting for you to add your voice to its last line:

Let every creature that breathes praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!

— Psalm 150:6
